decisions.reason: Having survived a further year as a low-cost, close-to-core design variant in a growing market, it likely meets minimum aspiration levels and is cheap enough to retain.
This shower channel remains tightly aligned with the firm's core drainage offer and barrier-free bathroom trend, so management would keep it unless results clearly fell below aspiration.

The pump-assisted range is still the most exposed because its niche and technical complexity can miss aspiration levels, but continued strategic relevance and available slack make retention more likely than withdrawal.
As a design-led complement to the established portfolio with limited additional organisational burden, it is likely to stay while the firm broadens its architectural offer.

Because this newer pump-drain channel still has uncertain market feedback but builds on the core business and recent development effort, management would usually keep it for another year of learning rather than drop it now.
